When the signal is discharged the electric organ will be negatively loaded compared to the head and an electric field is created around the fish. ( ) A weak electric current is created also in ordinary muscle cells when they contract. ( ) The fish varies the signals by changing the form of the electric field or the frequency of the signal discharge. ( ) In species that produce weak signals, an electric organ discharge, traveling from tail to head, creates a weak electric field around the fish. ( ) It is much weaker than in species like the electric eel, which can produce 600-volt discharges that stun prey. ( ) Any other organism entering the electric field will cause a distortion that is picked up by the electric sense organs in the fish's skin.
